paragraphs: Rav Minyomi son of Rav Nachumi [א), source footnote marker; footnote text not supplied].

Hyman calls him a leading sage of his generation in Rav Yosef’s time, citing [Ketubot 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.81b.7-11): A certain man had a yevamah fall to him in Pumbedita—Rav Yosef said—Abaye said to him—he sent it before R’ Chanina bar Papi (to the Land of Israel); he sent it back according to Rav Yosef. They sent it before Rav Minyomi son of Rav Nachumi; he sent it back according to Abaye: “And if Rav Yosef gives another reason for it, send it to me.” Again they sent it before Rav Minyomi son of Rav Nachumi. He said to him, “Rav Yosef bar Minyomi said as follows in the name of R’ Nachman,” etc.

In [Bava Metzia 109b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.109b.6) he says, “In a place where the planter takes half,” etc. He also says there, “Kupa saba—half,” etc. From this Hyman infers that he was one of the city’s judges.[^4]

notes.text: Kupa saba is retained as an unresolved phrase, not a newly invented sage named Kufa the Elder. The requested Bava Metzia response failed, and no reading is inferred from that failure.

The single selected Davidson Bava Metzia 109b digital scalar was freshly read whole (359 characters). It contains both planter-half and קופא סבא—half statements with full Rav Minyomi and full Rav Nachumi. Hyman supplies קופה, beside digital קופא; this is not proof of a letter-repair history. The older failed request and unavailable-evidence notes remain historical; the new exact scalar supplies additive evidence, not a retrospective PASS. No whole Ketubot scalar was newly inspected, so Chanina and Nachman there retain R-prime and no title is transferred from Bava Metzia. The source’s א) is a footnote marker with no supplied footnote text, not an ordinal I. Hyman calls him a leading sage of the generation. The referral is to the Land of Israel; the repeated father, imperative send to me and singular he said to him are preserved. The city-judge claim is Hyman’s inference. Kup(a) saba remains untranslated, not an independently identified elder. All source holds remain.

In Ketubot 81b, Chanina bar Papi sends a ruling in accord with Rav Yosef, and Minyomi sends one in accord with Abaye. The consulted text uses the plural “he said to them” at the end and explicitly names Rav Nachman. Hyman’s shorter quotation has the singular and an abbreviated title. In Bava Metzia 109b, the consulted text reads קופא סבא. Rashi there explains the phrase as a grapevine that has grown old in the vineyard, from which the planter takes a half share on the terms he describes. The claim that Minyomi was a city judge is Hyman’s inference.

The Ketubot text has Minyomi answer the messengers in the plural and names Rav Nachman in the transmission. Bava Metzia reads קופא סבא, where Hyman has קופה סבא. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Metzia.109b.6.1) explains it as a grapevine that has aged in the vineyard. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2504&lang=en) cites both passages and raises a separate question about Minyomi’s chronology.
